Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): share a single ImportManager for CopySourceToTcb shims
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://angular.dev/tools/devtools/contributing#commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [x] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

In `InliningMode.CopySourceToTcb`, `TypeCheckContextImpl.executeOperations` instantiated its own `ImportManager` when transforming the copied source, while `TypeCheckFile.render()` finalized a second `ImportManager` (initialized against an empty `contextFile`) for the same `.ngtypecheck.ts` shim file.

Because both `ImportManager` instances operated independently on the same output file:
1. Both started generating namespace imports at `i0`, producing conflicting `import * as i0` declarations for different modules (e.g., an external directive module and `@angular/core`).
2. `ensureTypeCheckFilePreparationImports` could not see or reuse existing imports in the copied source (such as `import {Component} from '@angular/core'`), emitting duplicate imports in the middle of the shim file.
3. `TypeCheckFile.contextFile` was created with empty text (`''`), so its `ImportManager` was unaware of existing `i0` identifiers in the copied source.
4. Newly inserted imports in `executeOperations` lacked a trailing newline, concatenating imports onto the first line of the file.

Issue Number: #71547
Alternative to #71558

## What is the new behavior?

`TypeCheckFile` and `TypeCheckContextImpl.executeOperations` now share `TypeCheckFile.importManager` and `TypeCheckFile.contextFile` (populated with the copied source text via `setCopiedSourceOrigin`) when generating a `CopySourceToTcb` shim:
- All imports for the shim file (from inline TCB operations, non-inline TCBs, and preparation imports) are managed by a single `ImportManager` and finalized once.
- Existing imports and identifiers in the copied source are properly reused and respected when generating unique namespace identifiers.
- Inserted imports include a trailing newline.
- `generateCopiedShimContent` runs before collecting `genesisDiagnostics` so DOM schema and out-of-band diagnostics produced during copied inline TCB generation are not lost.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): unconditionally use namespace imports for imported constructor tokens in ngp
Issues.Body:
Stacked on top of #71343.

### Description
In `ngp`, constructor dependency tokens and class metadata previously emitted bare identifiers (`SomeService`) for imported tokens from non-core modules in default `.ng.ts` emit, and only emitted namespace imports (`i1.SomeService`) when `complianceMode` was enabled.

This PR aligns `ngp` with `ngtsc` by unconditionally emitting imported constructor tokens and metadata through module namespace imports (`o.importExpr(...)`) whenever `param.typeModule != null`:
- Simplifies `buildDeps` by removing the `complianceMode` parameter.
- Simplifies `buildCtorParametersExpr` by removing the `useCoreNamespace` and `complianceMode` options.
- Updates affected preprocessor test goldens.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): decouple preprocessor HybridCompiler from tsconfigPath
Issues.Body:
`HybridCompiler` wrote `<tsconfig>.ngdiag.json` itself from `prepareChunk` and `prepareChunkSync`, which tied it to a `tsconfigPath` and to the Node filesystem, or to a `virtualFiles` overlay standing in for it. Now that the analyzer no longer requires a tsconfig, hosts that embed the compiler without one have nowhere to write such a file, and whether and where diagnostics are persisted is a decision for the build driver rather than for the compiler.

`tsconfigPath` and `virtualFiles` are therefore removed from `HybridCompilerOptions`, together with `writeDiagnosticsFile` and `writeDiagnosticsFileSync`, and `hybrid_compiler.ts` no longer imports `node:fs`. In their place, `HybridCompiler.getDiagnostics()` returns the collected per-file diagnostics in the deterministic order the `.ngdiag.json` already used and leaves out diagnostics anchored on `.d.ts` files unless `includeDeclarationFiles` is set, making it the single place that filters and orders them; `serializeDiagnostics` now only formats that output. The `.ngdiag.json` write moves into `run` in `ngp.ts`, gated on a new optional `RunOptions.tsconfigPath`. The write that preceded the processing of each chunk is dropped as redundant, while `run` still writes after every chunk and once more at the end so that option diagnostics reach the file even when the analyzer produces no chunks.

Without a tsconfig there is also nothing to resolve relative paths against, so `rootDir` and `rootDirs` on `HybridCompilerOptions` must now be absolute; relative `rootDirs` used to be resolved against `rootDir` or `dirname(tsconfigPath)`. This matters because `getProjectRelativePath`, which produces the `ɵsetClassDebugInfo` paths and HMR IDs, uses `path.posix.relative` and would silently resolve a relative root against the process cwd. Both options are normalized to forward slashes; `rootDir` previously was not, which would have broken that computation for backslash paths on Windows. `main.ts` resolves relative `rootDirs` against the tsconfig directory, matching TypeScript and the analyzer, and the test helpers do the same.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): implement uninvoked extended diagnostics in preprocessor
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [x] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

In NGP (`packages/compiler-cli/preprocessor`), extended template diagnostics run without an in-process `ts.TypeChecker` (designed to support out-of-process TypeScript 7 / `tsgo`). Consequently, the four type-dependent "uninvoked" extended diagnostics were unimplemented (or limited to AST-only arrow/function literals in `NG8111`):

- `interpolatedSignalNotInvoked` (`NG8109`)
- `uninvokedFunctionInEventBinding` (`NG8111`, property/method reads)
- `uninvokedTrackFunction` (`NG8115`)
- `uninvokedFunctionInTextInterpolation` (`NG8117`)

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

Implements all four uninvoked extended diagnostics in the NGP preprocessor via **`.ngtypecheck.ts` type-level probes + diagnostic remapping**:

1. **Private `@angular/core` type-checking helpers (`packages/core/src/type_checking.ts`):**
   - Exposes `@codeGenApi` helpers `ɵassertNotSignal`, `ɵassertNotCallable`, and `ɵassertNotTrackCallable` alongside `ɵassertType` (using `Signal<unknown>` directly and non-distributive conditional types so `any`, `never`, `unknown`, and nullable unions do not produce false positives, with zero per-file declaration boilerplate in `.ngtypecheck.ts` and zero runtime bundle impact).
2. **Candidate collection (`ExtendedTemplateCheckerImpl`):**
   - Extended checks register `TcbExtendedCheckCandidate` entries (`notSignal`, `notCallable`, `notTrackCallable`) with their configured category, pre-formatted `NG8xxx` message, template span, and optional `skipIfTriggered` superseding link (for `NG8109`'s signal/function instance property fallback such as `mySignal.name` / `mySignal.set`).
3. **TCB probe injection & metadata footer (`tcb_ls_util.ts` / `tcb.ts`):**
   - Resolves candidate expressions inside `_tcbN` via trailing span comments (preserving narrowing inside `if`/`switch` and guarding ternary conditional branches).
   - Injects `i1.ɵassertNotSignal(id, expr)`, `i1.ɵassertNotCallable(id, expr)`, and `i1.ɵassertNotTrackCallable(id, expr)` calls using the `@angular/core` namespace import.
   - Emits a `/*ngp-tcb-extended-checks:[...]*/` metadata footer in `.ngtypecheck.ts` so external diagnostic consumers remain completely stateless and require no `ts.TypeChecker` API calls.
4. **Diagnostic remapping & LS filtering (`diagnostic_mapping.ts`, `references_and_rename*.ts`, `ngp_test_driver.ts`):**
   - Remaps `TS2345` errors raised on probe arguments to their Angular extended diagnostic (`code`, `Warning`/`Error` severity, `message`, and exact template span, including external-template `relatedInformation`).
   - Suppresses secondary TypeScript diagnostics (e.g. `TS2339`) inside copied probe expressions so errors on the underlying TCB expression are never duplicated.
   - Filters synthetic probe occurrences out of Language Service Find References and Rename results.
5. **Known limitation:** Distinguishing a 0-arg class method on a `@for` loop variable (`track item.getId`) from a 0-arg callable property (`track field`, e.g. Signal Forms `Field<T>`) cannot be expressed purely at the TypeScript type level (`ts.SymbolFlags.Method` vs `ts.SymbolFlags.Property` have identical structural types `() => K`). Component methods (`track getId`) are flagged via `notCallable`, while other expressions use `notTrackCallable` (flagging `>= 1` required-arg functions while avoiding false positives on 0-arg callable properties).

Removes 75 passing extended diagnostic test cases from `ngp_known_failures.ts` (`NGP_REQUIRES_TYPE_CHECKER`) and adds end-to-end Language Service tests against TypeScript 7 (`tsgo`).

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(compiler-cli): implement uninvoked extended diagnostics in preprocessor" (#71650)

Issues.Title: fix(core): infer WebMCP tool argument types per tool
Issues.Body:
`provideExperimentalWebMcpTools` declared a single generic `InputSchema` shared by the whole `ToolDescriptor<InputSchema>[]` array. When tools with heterogeneous input schemas were provided together, TypeScript unified the schemas and the `execute` callbacks lost their argument types, so accessing the arguments produced type errors. Tools declared individually with `declareExperimentalWebMcpTool` were not affected.

The parameter is now a tuple-mapped type over the inferred schemas, so each tool infers its own `InputSchema` from its own `inputSchema` property. The call shape and the runtime behavior are unchanged, and homogeneous call sites compile as before.

Fixes #70125

- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`provideExperimentalWebMcpTools` declares a single generic `InputSchema` shared by the whole `ToolDescriptor<InputSchema>[]` array. With tools that have heterogeneous input schemas, TypeScript unifies the schemas and the `execute` callbacks lose their argument types (e.g. `args.arg1` resolves to `unknown`), producing type errors for
code that is correct at runtime.

The parameter is a tuple-mapped type over the inferred schemas, so each tool infers its own `InputSchema` from its own `inputSchema` property. The call shape and the runtime behavior are unchanged, and homogeneous call sites compile as before. A compile-time regression test in `packages/core/test/strict_types` fails with the old signature and passes with the fix.

Issues.Title: fix(core): do not treat outputs named class or style as styling inputs
Issues.Body:
Fixes #71660 | Regressed in #60036

## Why the change

When a directive has an output named `class` or `style`, Angular sends the template's `[class]` or `[style]` value to directive inputs that don't exist, so the value is silently dropped. With this fix, only real inputs with those names take over the binding.

## Special things to note

- This is a regression from #60036, first released in 19.2.0. That refactor moved the flag into per-binding helpers that both inputs and outputs share. Restoring the old code, which set the flag after collection by checking `tNode.inputs`, would also fix it. This fix keeps the helpers that #60036 introduced and only sets the flag on the input path.
- Inputs named `class` or `style` still take over the binding as before. A test covers a directive that has both an input and an output named `class`.
- Apps with such an output will now see the bound classes or styles, which matches the behavior before 19.2.0.

## Change outline

`setShadowStylingInputFlags` now runs only while inputs are being collected:

```diff
 initializeInputAndOutputAliases(tNode)
   for each directive on the node
     setupSelectorMatchedInputsOrOutputs(Inputs)
       setShadowStylingInputFlags          // input 'class' → hasClassInput
     setupSelectorMatchedInputsOrOutputs(Outputs)
-      setShadowStylingInputFlags          // output 'class' → hasClassInput too
     setupHostDirectiveInputsOrOutputs(Inputs)
       setShadowStylingInputFlags
     setupHostDirectiveInputsOrOutputs(Outputs)
-      setShadowStylingInputFlags
```

For a template binding, the flag decides where `[class]="cls()"` goes:

```text
ɵɵclassMap(cls())
  if hasClassInput
    write to directive inputs named 'class'   ← an output alone left none, so the value was lost
  else
    apply the classes to the element
```

The tests in `packages/core/test/acceptance/styling_spec.ts`:

```text
should not treat outputs named class or style as shadowing [class] and [style]   fails before the fix
should not treat a host directive output exposed as class as shadowing [class]   fails before the fix
should bind [class] as input to directive that also has an output named class    passes before and after
```

## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features). Not needed: this restores documented behavior.

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

An output named `class` or `style` makes a template `[class]` or `[style]` binding on the same element do nothing. Interpolated `class` and `style` attributes are affected too, and so are host directives that expose such an output.

Issue Number: #71660

## What is the new behavior?

These bindings are applied to the element. Only directive inputs named `class` or `style` take them over.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

This is a candidate for the patch branch, because the regression dates back to 19.2.0.

Issues.Title: `[class]` and `[style]` bindings are dropped when a directive has an output named `class` or `style`
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? core ### Is this a regression? Yes. It works in 19.1.x and is broken from 19.2.0 onward. ### Description When a directive on an element declares an output whose public name is `class`, the template's `[class]` binding on that element never reaches the DOM. Static classes and `[class.foo]` bindings still work. The same happens with an output named `style` and `[style]`. Nothing is reported at compile time or at runtime. ```ts @Directive({selector: '[dir]'}) export class Dir { @Output('class') out = new EventEmitter(); } @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [Dir], template: `
`, }) export class App { cls = signal('b'); } ``` Expected classes on the `div`: `b p s`, which is what you get without `dir`. Actual classes: `p s`. After `cls.set('b2')`, they are still `p s`. These forms are affected too: - `[style]` with an output named `style`. - Interpolated `class="s {{x}}"` and `style="width: {{w}}px"`. - Signal outputs, such as `output({alias: 'class'})`. - Host directives that expose an output as `class`, such as `outputs: ['out: class']`. `[className]`, `[class.foo]`, host bindings and `(class)` listeners still work. Cause: `setShadowStylingInputFlags` in `packages/core/src/render3/view/directives.ts` sets `TNodeFlags.hasClassInput`/`hasStyleInput` for outputs as well as inputs. The `[class]` value is then routed to directive inputs named `class`. None exist, so the value is dropped. This started with #60036, a refactor that moved the flag into helpers shared by inputs and outputs. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug No hosted reproduction. The snippet in the description is self-contained: paste it into any Angular 19.2+ app. The linked PR adds regression tests. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true None. The binding is dropped silently. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular: 19.2.0 and later, including angular/angular main at 8260542ce0. Reproduced with acceptance tests in packages/core/test/acceptance (AOT and JIT). ``` ### Anything else? A PR with a fix and regression tests follows: the flag is set only while collecting inputs.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): make tsconfig optional for the preprocessor analyzer
Issues.Body:
Integrations such as bundlers and the Angular CLI may have no tsconfig at all, or already own
the parsed configuration. The analyzer can now be constructed from options alone.

`AnalyzerOptions.tsconfigPath` is now optional, and three options replace what could
previously only come from the tsconfig:

- `entryPoints`: the roots of the program closure. When set, they replace the tsconfig's root
  files, and the roots are no longer re-read from the tsconfig after file updates (the same
  holds after `setEntryPoints`). Bundlers pass their own entry files; the analyzer follows
  imports from there. The `.d.ts` files a tsconfig lists are still searched for ambient
  modules either way.
- `r3SymbolsFile`: the `r3_symbols.ts` file used when compiling `@angular/core` itself, which
  was only found by scanning the root files for that name. The scan remains the fallback.
- `implicitStandalone`: whether declarations without an explicit `standalone` flag are
  standalone, which was only derived from `angularCompilerOptions._angularCoreVersion`. The
  tsconfig value remains the fallback, and the default is `true`.

`setEntryPoints` is now exposed on every backend (N-API, WASM and the sidecar) and on
`IAnalyzer`, so integrations that discover entry files incrementally can replace the roots
after construction. Like `updateFileContent`, it returns every path whose cached analysis is
now stale.

`createAnalyzer` and `createAnalyzerWithInfo` also accept a single options object in which
`tsconfigPath` is optional, alongside the existing tsconfig-path form, which is unchanged.

Without a tsconfig, every unset option takes its documented default (matching the defaults of
an empty tsconfig), path-valued options must be absolute since there is no directory to
resolve them against, and the module resolver runs without tsconfig `paths` mappings.
Behavior is unchanged when a tsconfig is given and the new options are unset.

Issues.Title: fix(forms): keep field cleanup from materializing unused children
Issues.Body:
## What is the current behavior?

Fixes #70627.

The field cleanup effect calls `children()`, which forces unused descendants to materialize. A large model with no child rules therefore creates a complete field tree on the first effect flush and blocks the page.

## What is the new behavior?

Walk `materializedChildren()` during cleanup. Explicit field access and schema logic continue to create fields as before.

The regression tests cover laziness after effects flush and model updates, unread descendants of an accessed field, cleanup of fields first accessed after the initial sweep, identity across array reordering, and validation of fields with rules. Two tests fail with the original traversal.

### Production-page measurements

Used the [reporter's application](https://github.com/ShacharHarshuv/angular-form-bug/tree/5f25e1cdd34cd351a844590be218af33082d0058) with Angular 22.2.3, CLI/build 22.2.4, Node 24.22.1, and Chrome Headless 158.0.8117.0. Both optimized builds use identical instrumentation; the patched build changes only this traversal in the installed forms bundle.

For 10,000 rows, five alternating baseline/patched pairs in fresh browser contexts:

| Metric (median) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Form constructor to next timer, including the initial effect flush | 561.8 ms | 3.8 ms |
| Materialized child fields | 50,000 | 0 |
| Additional live JS heap after forced GC | 372,986,828 B | 679,972 B |

The baseline produced a 536–627 ms long task in every run; the patched run produced no long task over 50 ms. Model allocation happens before the measured action. These are local page measurements, not INP or device-independent guarantees.

Control: 50 rendered inputs with `required()`, seven alternating pairs. Medians were 29.6 ms before / 28.7 ms after; both created 250 child fields, and editing updated the model in every run. The patched app also completed the reporter's original 100,000-row case in three runs without materializing children. The baseline was measured at 10,000 rows rather than run to exhaustion at 100,000.

### Validation

- Signal forms Node suite: 546 specs, 0 failures.
- Signal forms Chromium suite: 362 specs, 0 failures. The local runner needed a loopback-interface shim because the container rejects `os.networkInterfaces()`; that shim is outside this change.
- Regression check with the original traversal: 2 failures among the 5 lazy-materialization specs.
- `ng-dev format`, Prettier, and `git diff --check` pass.

Related prior work: #70633 and #71635.

- [x] Tests for the changes have been added.
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated: no public API or documented behavior changes.

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(forms): reject unsupported updateOn in SignalFormControl
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

This was caught while reviewing #70735. This is mostely to warn users that might be suprised by the (lack of) behavior.

## What is the current behavior?

`SignalFormControl` does not support pending or uncommitted values because signal forms are model-driven and react immediately on change. When placed in a `FormGroup` or `FormArray` configured with `updateOn: 'blur'` or `updateOn: 'submit'`, or when initialized with `updateOn` options, `SignalFormControl` would inherit or receive the unsupported option, causing split-brain states or broken submit syncing.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

This commit adds a dev-mode check in `SignalFormControl` to throw an error when:
1. An unsupported `updateOn` option is passed directly in options to the `SignalFormControl` constructor.
2. A non-default `updateOn` option is inherited from a parent `FormGroup` or `FormArray` via `setParent()`.

Additionally, `SignalFormControl` explicitly overrides `get updateOn()` to return `'change'`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Issues.Title: fix(core): prevent window.opener exposure in sanitized HTML links
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

The HTML sanitizer allowlists both `rel` and `target` attributes without filtering `rel` tokens or accounting for custom named `target` browsing contexts. Consequently, untrusted HTML passed through `[innerHTML]` or `DomSanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, ...)` can retain `rel="opener"` (which opts out of modern browsers' implicit `noopener` default on `target="_blank"`) or specify a custom `target` window name (which does not receive implicit `noopener`), exposing `window.opener` to newly opened tabs.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

- Strips the `opener` token (ASCII case-insensitively across ASCII whitespace) from `rel` attributes in `SanitizingHtmlSerializer` (omitting `rel` completely if `opener` was its sole token, and recording `sanitizedSomething = true`).
- Ensures `noopener` is present in `rel` (unless `noopener` or `noreferrer` is already present) on `<a>` and `<area>` elements with custom `target` browsing context names (any non-empty value other than `_blank`, `_self`, `_parent`, or `_top`), while leaving standard `target="_blank"` without `rel="opener"` untouched.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): keep the default getter access type of spyOnProperty in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

`refactor-jasmine-vitest` drops default access type of `spyOnProperty`
Jasmine uses `'get'` when third argument is missing, `vi.spyOn` without it is typed and run as method spy

This spec passes on Jasmine:

```ts
class Session {
  get user(): string {
    return 'real';
  }
}

it('stubs the getter', () => {
  const session = new Session();
  spyOnProperty(session, 'user').and.returnValue('mocked');
  expect(session.user).toBe('mocked');
});
```

`ng g @schematics/angular:refactor-jasmine-vitest` on 22.3.0-next.3 turns it into `vi.spyOn(session, 'user').mockReturnValue('mocked')` and `ng test` fails to build:

```
✘ [ERROR] TS2769: No overload matches this call.
```

Without type check Vitest throws `vi.spyOn() can only spy on a function` at runtime

## What is the new behavior?

`transformPrimarySpy` adds `'get'` when `spyOnProperty` has two arguments, explict access type is kept as is
Same spec converts to `vi.spyOn(session, 'user', 'get').mockReturnValue('mocked')` and passes under `ng test`

Existing case in `jasmine-spy_spec.ts` expected `vi.spyOn(service, 'myProp').mockReturnValue(undefined)` for bare `spyOnProperty`, so it pinned this output
Updated it and added two cases, chained one and explicit `'set'`, updated and chained ones fail on main

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Bare `spyOnProperty(obj, 'prop')` still gets `.mockReturnValue(undefined)` from #33266, so after this change it compiles only when getter type allows `undefined`, same as bare `spyOn` on method that returns `string`

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

<!-- Please check all that apply using "x". -->

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes

## What is the current behavior?

`filter()` only accepts a `HostTree` and throws "Tree type is not supported." for anything else. A `UnitTestTree` is a `DelegateTree` around a `HostTree`, so a schematic that uses `filter()` fails in unit tests when it runs on the tree returned by an earlier `runSchematic` call.

Issue Number: #26000

## What is the new behavior?

`filter()` and `partition()` (behind `partitionApplyMerge`) call `branch()` on a delegating tree first, which returns a branch of the `HostTree` it wraps. Other tree types still throw as before.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

The new specs in `base_spec.ts` cover `filter` on a plain `HostTree` (it had no spec) and `filter` and `partitionApplyMerge` on a nested `UnitTestTree`, since `runSchematic` returns a `UnitTestTree` around another one when the schematic edits its input tree in place. Locally, the `UnitTestTree` specs fail on `main` with "Tree type is not supported." and pass with this change, and the 86 specs under `src/rules` and `src/tree` pass (run with jasmine, not Bazel).


Closes #26000

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): include the oxc-parser WASI binding as an optional dependency
Issues.Body:
When running inside a WebContainer environment, such as StackBlitz or the angular.dev playground, native Node.js addons cannot be loaded. The `oxc-parser` package only lists its platform-specific native bindings as optional dependencies and does not include the WebAssembly-based `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` binding. As a result, package managers never install the WASI binding and `oxc-parser` falls back to downloading it on demand at runtime by shelling out to `pnpm` inside a temporary directory. This fallback is executed synchronously while the module graph is being evaluated, from within a worker thread, and via a synchronous `require()` of an ES module. Any failure along that path surfaces as a misleading `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE` error rather than the underlying cause, which breaks `ng serve` and `ng build` entirely.

The binding loader generated by napi-rs checks whether the WASI binding is already resolvable from `node_modules` before attempting the on-demand download. Declaring `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` as an optional dependency of `@angular/build` ensures that package managers install it alongside the package up front. This allows `oxc-parser` to load the WASI binding directly in WebContainer environments and avoids the fragile runtime installation path. The version is pinned to match `oxc-parser` exactly, since the loader rejects bindings whose version does not match the version of the main package. The two dependencies must therefore be kept in lockstep when updating.

Note that at the time of this change, the currently published WASI bindings for `oxc-parser` depend on an `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime` version range that resolves to a release incompatible with the `@emnapi` alpha runtime those bindings were built against. Until a compatible `oxc-parser` release is available, the pre-installed binding will fail to initialize in the same way the on-demand download does. This change is nonetheless a prerequisite for a durable fix and will take effect once `oxc-parser` is updated to a release with compatible WASI bindings.

Related to #34524
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/build): include the oxc-parser WASI binding as an optional dependency" (#34540)

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): migrate CallInfo returnValue and object in refactor-jasmine-vitest
Issues.Body:
Previously, only the `.args` property of a Jasmine `CallInfo` object obtained via `spy.calls.first()`, `spy.calls.mostRecent()`, or `spy.calls.all()[i]` was migrated. Accessing `.returnValue` or `.object` on these results left the property intact on the transformed `mock.calls[i]` tuple, producing code that fails type checking and throws at runtime.

These properties are now mapped to the corresponding Vitest `MockContext` members:

- `spy.calls.first().returnValue`      -> `vi.mocked(spy).mock.results[0].value`
- `spy.calls.all()[i].returnValue`     -> `vi.mocked(spy).mock.results[i].value`
- `spy.calls.mostRecent().returnValue` -> `vi.mocked(spy).mock.results.at(-1)?.value`
- `spy.calls.first().object`           -> `vi.mocked(spy).mock.contexts[0]`
- `spy.calls.all()[i].object`          -> `vi.mocked(spy).mock.contexts[i]`
- `spy.calls.mostRecent().object`      -> `vi.mocked(spy).mock.contexts.at(-1)`

The separate `transformMostRecentArgs` and `transformAllCallsArgs` handlers have been consolidated into a single `transformCallInfoProperty` transformer, and the TODO for a bare `mostRecent()` call no longer fires when one of the supported properties is accessed.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): support resolving subproject dependencies in bun workspaces
Issues.Body:
When running `bun pm ls` inside a workspace member directory, Bun resolves the workspace root lockfile and outputs only the direct dependencies declared in the root `package.json`, along with `workspace:` references to member packages. Because subproject dependencies (such as `@angular/core`) are omitted from this output, commands like `ng update` and `ng add` fail to detect installed project dependencies when executed in a Bun workspace member.

To resolve this, `parseBunDependencies` now ignores `workspace:` protocol entries, and the `bun` package manager descriptor enables `requiresManifestDependencyLookup`. When populating the dependency cache, `PackageManager` supplements the command output by reading `dependencies` and `devDependencies` from the working directory's `package.json` and resolving their installed manifests across ancestor `node_modules` directories up to the workspace lockfile or repository root. Additionally, `getPackageNameCommand` is configured for `bun` using `bun pm pkg get name` to provide the same CLI fallback as `npm` and `pnpm`.

Fixes #34402

Issues.Title: perf(@angular/build): avoid duplicate Domino bundling in server bundles
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

[✓] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
[✓] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
[ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

[ ] Bugfix
[✓] Feature / Performance
[ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
[ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
[ ] Build related changes
[ ] CI related changes
[ ] Documentation content changes
[ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When bundling an application with server-side rendering, Domino (~560 KB unminified) is bundled into both `polyfills.server.mjs` (via `@angular/platform-server/init`) and `main.server.mjs` (via `@angular/platform-server`).

## What is the new behavior?

Domino is bundled only once in `polyfills.server.mjs` and attached to `globalThis['ɵdomino']`. The main server bundle redirects Domino imports to this shared instance.

This replaces the redundant bundled copy of Domino in `main.server.mjs` without requiring manual filesystem probing or `additionalContent` parameter threading in polyfill options.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

[ ] Yes
[✓] No

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

`refactor-jasmine-vitest` turns `spy.calls.first()` into `vi.mocked(spy).mock.calls[0]`, which is argumnets array of first call, and keeps `.args` that follows it
So `expect(spy.calls.first().args[0]).toBe(1)` becomes `expect(vi.mocked(spy).mock.calls[0].args[0]).toBe(1)` and converted spec does not build with `ng test` (checked on 22.3.0-next.3):

```
✘ [ERROR] TS2339: Property 'args' does not exist on type '[id: number, flag?: boolean | undefined]'. [plugin angular-compiler]
```

Without type check it throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')`
`mostRecent().args` and `all()[i].args` (#33206) already drop `.args`, only `first()` was missed

## What is the new behavior?

`spy.calls.first().args` becomes `vi.mocked(spy).mock.calls[0]`, in same transformer that handles `mostRecent().args`
Same spec after conversion builds and passes with `ng test`
Two new cases in `jasmine-spy_spec.ts`, both fail on main

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: ci: update e2e runs-on to ubuntu-24.04
Issues.Body:
The `ubuntu-latest` runner image recently began migrating to Ubuntu 26.04, which mounts `/tmp` as a 7.8 GB `tmpfs` RAM disk with a per-user disk quota. This causes large builds and package extraction (such as yarn in E2E tests) to fail with `EDQUOT` (disk quota exceeded).

See: https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14777

This commit pins `runs-on` to `ubuntu-24.04` for the E2E test jobs.

### [`v8.12.2`](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/releases/tag/v8.12.2)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v8.12.1...v8.12.2)

##### Security fixes

##### High severity

##### Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

**CVE-2026-87018 · [GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm)**

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

##### TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped `Agent` options

**CVE-2026-109383 · [GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx)**

`Agent` used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as `checkServerIdentity`. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

##### Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

**CVE-2026-109829 · [GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26)**

When an originless `Agent` combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as `compose(redirect(), cache())`, a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

##### Denial of service through excessive `Content-Encoding` values

**CVE-2026-109869 · [GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c)**

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although `fetch()` rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

##### Medium severity

##### Denial of service through the `decompress` interceptor

**CVE-2026-87029 · [GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6)**

An exception thrown by a downstream response handler from an asynchronous decompression callback could escape as an uncaught exception. A server could trigger this when `decompress` was composed with a handler such as `dump` with a size limit. This release converts downstream handler exceptions into per-request errors.

##### Subresource Integrity bypass with non-lowercase algorithm tokens

**CVE-2026-109841 · [GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472)**

`fetch()` treated valid mixed-case or uppercase SRI algorithm tokens, such as `SHA256`, as unknown and could accept a response whose body did not match the configured digest. This release normalizes algorithm tokens before validation and digest selection.

##### Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

**CVE-2026-109924 · [GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685)**

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny `data:` fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

##### Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

**CVE-2026-109932 · [GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6)**

A malicious WebSocket server could exhaust process memory by flooding the client with PING frames while not reading the automatic PONG responses. undici previously ignored socket backpressure and allowed the outbound queue to grow without bound. This release pauses frame parsing when PONG writes encounter backpressure and resumes after the socket drains.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v8.12.1...v8.12.2>

Issues.Title: build: ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE when loading oxc-parser in StackBlitz / WebContainer
Issues.Body:
### Command
build, serve

### Is this a regression?
Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### Description
In StackBlitz (WebContainer), running an Angular application with `@angular/build` fails during `ng serve` / `ng build` with:

```
(node:12) ExperimentalWarning: WASI is an experimental feature and might change at any time
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
[oxc-parser] Downloading @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.150.0 on WebContainer...
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE]: Cannot require() ES Module /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/oxc-parser/src-js/index.js in a cycle. (from /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/@angular/build/src/tools/oxc/oxc-transform.js) A cycle involving require(esm) is not allowed to maintain invariants mandated by the ECMAScript specification. Try making at least part of the dependency in the graph lazily loaded.
    at ModuleLoader.importSyncForRequire (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:169:3960)
    at loadESMFromCJS (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:19002)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:19068)
    at Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:20043)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:17661)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:15179)
    at wrapModuleLoad (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:4199)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:17842)
    at require2 (node:internal/modules/helpers:177:3126) {
  code: 'ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE'
}
```

Parent issue: https://github.com/stackblitz/starters/issues/136

#### Analysis & Root Cause

1. **No actual cyclic dependency in the code:**
   The module graph (`oxc-transform.ts` -> `oxc-parser`, `oxc-transform.ts` -> `traversal.ts` -> `oxc-parser`) is an acyclic DAG.
   The `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE` error is a known misleading error in Node.js's synchronous `require(esm)` loader (Node.js issues [#55516](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/55516) and [#57172](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/57172)). When an ES module throws an error during synchronous `require(esm)` evaluation, Node's loader frequently shadows the real underlying exception and reports that the module was required in a cycle.

2. **WebContainer Fallback Failure:**
   - StackBlitz WebContainer cannot run native `.node` addons.
   - `oxc-parser`'s `optionalDependencies` only list platform-specific native addons (`@oxc-parser/binding-linux-x64-gnu`, etc.) and do not list `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi`. Consequently, package managers running in WebContainer never install the WASI binding.
   - At runtime, `oxc-parser/src-js/bindings.js` detects WebContainer and falls back to `webcontainer-fallback.cjs`, which attempts to run `childProcess.execFileSync("pnpm", ["i", "@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@..."], { cwd: "/tmp/..." })`.
   - Running this synchronous subprocess from a worker thread inside WebContainer fails (or fails to initialize the multi-threaded WASI runtime), causing the synchronous `require(esm)` evaluation of `oxc-parser` to fail and surface as `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE`.

#### Proposed Solution (Option 4A: Add `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` to `@angular/build` optionalDependencies)

In `oxc-parser/src-js/bindings.js`, before falling back to `webcontainer-fallback.cjs`, it checks:
```js
__napiWasiResolveCandidate('@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi', true, undefined)
```
If `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` is already present in `node_modules`, `oxc-parser` directly loads it and bypasses `webcontainer-fallback.cjs` and the dynamic `pnpm i` in `/tmp` entirely.

A viable solution (Option 4A) is to declare `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` in `@angular/build`'s `optionalDependencies` (similar to how `lmdb` is declared).
This ensures that package managers install the WASI binding up-front alongside `@angular/build`, preventing the runtime dynamic installation and the resulting failure in WebContainer.

### Minimal Reproduction
1. Open https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac?file=package.json (or update any StackBlitz Angular starter to Angular CLI v22.2+).
2. Run `npm install && npm start` (or `ng serve`).
3. Notice the build fails with `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE: Cannot require() ES Module .../oxc-parser/src-js/index.js in a cycle`.

### Exception or Error
```
(node:12) ExperimentalWarning: WASI is an experimental feature and might change at any time
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
[oxc-parser] Downloading @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.150.0 on WebContainer...
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE]: Cannot require() ES Module /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/oxc-parser/src-js/index.js in a cycle. (from /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/@angular/build/src/tools/oxc/oxc-transform.js) A cycle involving require(esm) is not allowed to maintain invariants mandated by the ECMAScript specification. Try making at least part of the dependency in the graph lazily loaded.
    at ModuleLoader.importSyncForRequire (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:169:3960)
    at loadESMFromCJS (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:19002)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:19068)
    at Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:20043)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:17661)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:15179)
    at wrapModuleLoad (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:4199)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:17842)

}

```

```
OS: linux x64 (WebContainer)
```

Issues.Title: bug(material/datepicker): Focus moves to a date cell instead of returning to the period button after selecting a year/month (WCAG 2.4.3)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

No, this behaviour has always existed.

### Description

When the calendar’s period button (“Choose month and year”) is activated by keyboard, the calendar switches to the multi-year view and then the year view. After the user selects a year and then a month, the calendar returns to the month view and focus moves to a date cell in the calendar grid. It does not return to the period button that opened the view.

This affects keyboard and screen reader users. They can’t easily change the month or year again, because the next Tab or Shift+Tab stop is unpredictable. They have to navigate back through the grid to reach the period button. We believe this fails WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order) in accessibility audits, because the focus destination after the interaction doesn’t preserve a logical, predictable order relative to the control that triggered it.

### Reproduction

This reproduces on the official Angular Material documentation example: https://material.angular.dev/components/datepicker/overview#datepicker-custom-icon

Steps to reproduce (keyboard only):
1.Open the datepicker with the “Open calendar” button (Enter).
2.Press Tab until the “Choose month and year” period button is focused, then press Enter.
3.Use the arrow keys to select a year and press Enter.
4.Use the arrow keys to select a month and press Enter.
5.Observe where focus lands.


### Expected Behavior

Focus returns to the period button that opened the view, so users can change the month/year again or Tab onward predictably. Alternatively, expose an option to control this, for example an input on mat-calendar.

### Actual Behavior

Focus moves to a date cell (.mat-calendar-body-cell) in the month grid. The period button loses focus and the user has to navigate back to it manually.

### Environment

- Angular: 19.2.14
- CDK/Material: 19.2.19
- Browser(s): Chrome, Safari
- Operating System : macOS

Issues.Title: Feature (MatDialog): Add an option to prevent duplicate dialogs
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

Currently, Angular Material’s MatDialog allows the same component to be opened multiple times, resulting in multiple instances of the same dialog being displayed simultaneously.

In some applications, this behavior is undesirable. For example, repeated user interactions or multiple event emissions can accidentally open the same dialog more than once.

Developers must currently implement their own duplicate detection logic using MatDialog.openDialogs or MatDialog.getDialogById() before calling MatDialog.open().

Proposed solution

It would be useful to have a built-in option in MatDialogConfig to prevent duplicate instances of the same component from being opened.

For example:

this.dialog.open(MyDialogComponent, {
  preventDuplicates: true,
});

When this option is enabled, attempting to open a component that already has an open dialog could either:

* Return the existing MatDialogRef without creating another instance.
* Ignore the new request and keep the existing dialog open.

The exact behavior could be determined by the maintainers.

Ideally, duplicate detection would be scoped to the component type, with an option to customize the behavior if needed.

Benefits

* Avoids accidentally opening multiple instances of the same dialog.
* Reduces repetitive boilerplate across applications.
* Provides a consistent, framework-level solution.
* Keeps applications simpler and less error-prone.

Alternatives considered

Currently, developers can manually inspect openDialogs or use getDialogById() before opening a dialog. However, this requires additional application-level logic and does not provide a straightforward, reusable option for this common use case.

Would this feature be a good fit for Angular Material’s MatDialog API? I’d be happy to contribute a PR if the maintainers consider this approach appropriate.

### Use Case

Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Pressing Enter on a link (or Space on a button) inside an expanded `ngAccordionPanel` collapses the panel instead of activating the link/button.

`ngAccordionGroup` handles `keydown` for the whole group, including panel content, and calls `preventDefault()` on Enter/Space, so the focused element never gets activated. Arrow keys and Home/End are affected too, e.g. Home in an input inside a panel moves focus to the trigger.

The click handler only reacts to events coming from a trigger (`_findTriggerPattern`), the keydown handler doesn't check that:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/952685f9370ba718f832d745512db7c9a04e1bcd/src/aria/private/accordion/accordion.ts#L73-L97

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/z5sxyaq6?file=src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Expand "Section 1".
2. Tab to "Link inside panel" or "Button inside panel" and press Enter / Space.
3. Expand it again, click into the input and press Home.

### Expected Behavior

The link/button is activated (shows up in the log) and the panel stays open. Home moves the caret in the input.

### Actual Behavior

The panel collapses, nothing is activated. Home moves focus to the trigger.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.3
- CDK/Material: @angular/aria 22.2.4 (also 22.1.6)
- Browser(s): Chrome 155
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Linux

Issues.Title: build: guard branch-manager against forks and harden checkout
Issues.Body:
This change restores `if: github.event.repository.fork == false` on `.github/workflows/assistant-to-the-branch-manager.yml` on the `22.2.x` branch per GHSS `pull_request_target` policy remediation (b/577107676).

Because 100% of pull requests in `angular/components` originate from forks (`only_allow_releasable_branches: true`) and `branch-manager` requires `context.eventName === 'pull_request_target'` along with `secrets.ANGULAR_ROBOT_PRIVATE_KEY` to set mergeability commit status, the previous `head.repo.fork == false` check caused all fork PR runs to be skipped. Restoring the base repository fork check ensures branch-manager triggers as intended on upstream PRs while preventing runs on external forks.

Additionally, `persist-credentials: false` is added to `actions/checkout` in `.github/workflows/google-internal-tests.yml` for defense-in-depth.

Issues.Title: bug(ClickEventManager): Clicks on iOS 18.2 and before do not have pointer type
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

I found this problem using the listbox component, but I am pretty sure all components that use the ClickEventManager have this problem. iOS versions older than 18.2 do not have a pointer type, the ClickEventManager sees these as fake clicks (see isFakeClick function) and ignores them, so clicks do not work.

See release notes about the pointer type.
https://webkit.org/blog/16301/webkit-features-in-safari-18-2/

### Reproduction

Can be reproduced on https://angular.dev with a iOS version older than 18.2, with multiple components for example on https://angular.dev/guide/aria/select.

### Expected Behavior

Clicks in components handeld via ClickEventManager on iOS version older than 18.2 should work.

### Actual Behavior

Clicks in components handled via ClickEventManager on iOS version older than 18.2 do not work.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.3
- CDK/Material: 22.2.3
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): iOS version older than 18.2

Issues.Title: fix(multiple): avoid duplicate required error with signal forms
Issues.Body:
When a checkbox or slide toggle is bound to a signal forms field whose schema uses `required()`, signal forms set the component's `required` input and also run the component's own validator. This resulted in two `required` errors, and the one from the component doesn't have the message from the schema, which hides it when using `getError('required')`.

These changes skip the component's `required` validation when it's bound to a signal forms field, since the schema already handles it.

Fixes #33945.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(multiple): avoid duplicate required error with signal forms" (#33990)

Issues.Title: fix(material/menu): do not pull focus out of an overlay opened by a menu item
Issues.Body:
When a menu item opens an overlay, like a dialog, that focuses its content before the menu closes (e.g. when animations are disabled), the menu would restore focus to its trigger behind the overlay. These changes skip restoring focus when the menu is closed by a click and focus has moved into a different overlay. Focus is still restored if it's in another menu (e.g. when clicking an item in a sub-menu), in the overlay containing the trigger, or outside of any overlay.

Fixes #33967.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(material/menu): do not pull focus out of an overlay opened by a menu item" (#33989)

Issues.Title: fix(aria/menu): avoid re-rendering when unrelated elements are added
Issues.Body:
Updates the `SortedCollection` so it doesn't emit changes when a DOM node that's not a member of the collection is added. I also did some internal cleanup so we don't need to re-create the `Set` all the time and to keep a version counter.

Fixes #33976.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(aria/menu): avoid re-rendering when unrelated elements are added" (#33996)

Issues.Title: fix(material/checkbox): duplicate required error with signal forms
Issues.Body:
The checkbox has a custom required error in template/reactive forms. When it's used together with the signal forms interop, it was causing double `required` errors to show up. These changes skip the custom validation when signal forms are present.

Also fixes a similar issue with the slide toggle.

Fixes #33945.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(material/checkbox): duplicate required error with signal forms" (#33998)

Issues.Title: docs(cdk/scrolling): explain how to react to scroll events
Issues.Body:
Adds a section to the scrolling overview that shows how to listen to scroll events with `cdkScrollable` and the `ScrollDispatcher`, along with a live example.

Fixes #9594 
The scrolling overview only had two short paragraphs about `cdkScrollable` and `ScrollDispatcher` and didn't show how to actually listen to scroll events. This adds:

- a section on `elementScrolled`, `scrolled` and `ancestorScrolled`, with a snippet
- a live example (`cdk-scrollable-overview`) that shows the scroll offset and scrolls back to the top
- a note that the events fire outside the Angular zone, so the view only updates if you use signals or `markForCheck`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs(cdk/scrolling): explain how to react to scroll events" (#33997)

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v12.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.15.0): pnpm 12.15

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.14.0...v12.15.0)

This release lets `pnpm-workspace.yaml` delegate settings to other files and config dependencies with `include`, adds `lockfile.integrityTarget: tar` and tar-registry support, accepts zstd-compressed registry responses, and honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` in `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install`. It also rejects registry metadata that names a different package than the one requested and speeds up workspace installs and macOS file linking.

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` can now delegate settings to other YAML files and to config dependencies through a new `include` field. Each source may define only the settings the root manifest delegates to it. Every setting has one owner. Commands that change settings write each one to the file that owns it. A relative path in an included file is relative to that file. See [Splitting Settings Across Files](https://pnpm.io/config-includes).

  A config dependency supplies its settings through the YAML file named in the `pnpm.config` field of its `package.json`. The new `bootConfig` setting sets the release-age and trust policy pnpm uses to install config dependencies and the pnpm version from `packageManager`.

- Added the `lockfile.integrityTarget` setting. With `integrityTarget: tar`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins the hash of every package's uncompressed tar, so the lockfile no longer changes when a registry recompresses its tarballs or serves them as tars. pnpm learns a version's tar hash from the store or by downloading it once. `pnpm audit signatures` ties the tar hash to the signed `.tgz` integrity.

  ```yaml title="pnpm-workspace.yaml"
  lockfile:
    integrityTarget: tar
  ```

- pnpm can now install from a registry that serves uncompressed tars with zstd or gzip content coding. `pnpm-lock.yaml` records the hash of each tar. Declare such a registry with `serverType: pnpr` in `registries` to keep tarball URLs out of the lockfile. See [Tar registries](https://pnpm.io/registries#tar-registries).

  pnpm now decodes the content coding of tarball downloads itself. It rejects a zstd response whose window is larger than 8 MiB.

  Added the `maxTarballUnpackedSize` setting. It caps the bytes the files of one package may unpack to, 4 GiB by default.

- Registry revisions now always pin the hash of the uncompressed tar, the original included. pnpm records an original selected through the revision protocol, for example with a `+r0` specifier, as `revision: 0` in the lockfile and fetches it from the registry's digest route. pnpm checks a revision's tar whether the registry sends it as a tar, gzip, or zstd. Revision metadata must list revision 0 and mark the selected revision. pnpm rejects incomplete revision metadata with `ERR_PNPM_MALFORMED_METADATA`.

- pnpm now accepts zstd-compressed responses. Registries that serve zstd send package metadata in fewer bytes than with gzip, most of all the full metadata that settings such as `minimumReleaseAge` and `trustPolicy` read.

- `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install` now use the `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable as an upper bound for timestamps in `node_modules/.modules.yaml` and `node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`. With an equivalently prepared deploy target and an epoch no later than the timestamps that would otherwise be recorded, deploying the same project twice produces identical files [#​17171](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17171).

- `pnpm update --interactive` now highlights the row under the cursor in cyan while keeping the colors of its version changes.

##### Patch Changes

##### Security

- pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_REGISTRY_NAME_MISMATCH` if a registry returns metadata for a package other than the one requested. Before, pnpm installed the package under the name in the metadata, so `allowBuilds` rules for the requested package did not apply to it.

- `minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune` and `trustPolicyExcludePrune` now keep exclusions for resolved configuration dependencies and their transitive dependencies [#​17142](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17142).

##### Resolving dependencies

- When `pnpm install` resolves a dependency again, it now reuses a version that the install already resolved for the same package, as a fresh install does. Before, it kept the version the lockfile pinned and added a second copy of the package. A locked version still stays when nothing else in the install prefers another version. To pin a transitive dependency on purpose, use `overrides` [#​17084](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17084).

- When another workspace project adds a different version of a package, a project's auto-installed peer on that package now moves to the version a fresh install picks. It used to stay on its locked version while any other project still accepted that version [#​17058](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17058).

- A package that lists the same dependency in `dependencies` and as an optional peer now gets the peer bound when a project adds a provider for it later. The lockfile now records every peer a package declares, including one its own dependency supplies [#​17056](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17056).

- `pnpm install --prod` and `pnpm deploy --prod` no longer drop a dependency that a package declares both as an optional peer and as its own dependency, when the package resolved it as its own dependency and a dev dependency provides the same package under another alias.

- `pnpm install` with an existing lockfile and a second `pnpm dedupe` now keep optional peer bindings that point into a dependency cycle or back into the dependent package. Before, the second run dropped the optional peer binding from the lockfile snapshot key.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` now preserve own-dependency and peer-dependency bindings when reusing a lockfile whose peer suffixes were hashed by `peersSuffixMaxLength`.

  Upgrading a direct dependency in one workspace project now refreshes matching transitive pins in sibling projects during the same `pnpm install` pass.

- With `resolvePeersFromWorkspaceRoot: false`, a workspace project no longer binds a peer to a version that only another project's dependencies provide. pnpm now auto-installs a version that satisfies the peer range for that project. Before, the project got a version outside the range, with no peer warning.

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm add`, and `pnpm update` now reuse the lockfile's resolution for dependencies that take part in a dependency cycle, such as `mlly` and `pkg-types`. They re-resolved those packages and everything that depends on them from the registry before [pnpm/tasks#130](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/130).

- pnpm now measures a `pnpm.overrides` entry written as a `workspace:` path, such as `workspace:./packages/foo`, from the directory holding `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. It used to be measured from each package the override rewrote. The install then linked a directory that does not exist, or failed if workspace packages were injected [#​17010](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17010).

- `pnpm install` now removes config dependencies that are no longer declared, including when the entire `configDependencies` setting is removed. Frozen installs reject a lockfile that still records removed config dependencies.

- `pnpm install --update-checksums` now re-resolves every locked package and records the integrity the registry reports now.

- `pnpm add` and `pnpm install` now accept `gist:<id>` dependencies and GitHub Gist URLs, and install them from the gist's archive. `pnpm pkg fix` normalizes a `gist:` repository the way `npm pkg fix` does, `pnpm licenses` links a gist package to its gist page, and `pnpm sbom` reports the repository of a package whose `repository` field is a `gist:` shorthand.

- `pnpm add` now reads the package name correctly from a tarball URL under a registry URL that has a path, such as `https://example.com/npm/`, and installs a registry tarball URL with a malformed percent escape as a plain tarball URL. Before, the registry path became part of the name, so a scoped package failed with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_PACKAGE_NAME`.

- With `minimumReleaseAge` set, pnpm now revalidates a package's cached full metadata with a single ETag request so an unchanged registry answers with `304`, even when the registry does not list a publish time for every version. Previously, pnpm downloaded that metadata again whenever the cached copy was older than `minimumReleaseAge`. With `resolutionMode` set to `lowest-direct` or `time-based`, pnpm also reuses that metadata across every workspace project that depends on the package.

- When pnpm revalidates cached registry metadata, it now sends `If-Modified-Since` when the registry's modification time is a date without a time, and no longer crashes when the modification time is before 1970.

- Added protocol versioning between the pnpm client and pnpr server, verified applied resolution policies in resolution responses, and preserved structured error codes across the wire.

##### Performance

- Sped up `pnpm install` on macOS. On a 12-core Mac, installing 1352 packages from a warm store took 1.3 seconds, down from 2.2. pnpm now writes package files into `node_modules` with 4 threads on macOS, whatever the number of CPU cores. Set the `PNPM_MACOS_LINK_THREADS` environment variable to use a different number of threads, or to `0` to write files with the threads pnpm uses for the rest of the install.

- `pnpm install` is faster and uses less memory in large workspaces with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. Each project's install no longer reads the manifests of every other workspace project again. Installs that wait for their workspace dependencies now count toward `workspaceConcurrency` [#​16966](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16966).

- Sped up workspace project discovery, dependency resolution, lockfile up-to-date checks, and peer dependency checks in large workspaces [#​16839](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16839) [pnpm/tasks#9](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/9). On a workspace with 6,833 projects, the lockfile up-to-date check uses about 1 second less CPU time. The peer dependency check at the end of an install now checks linked workspace projects against the manifests already in memory, without reading each `package.json` again.

- Sped up bin linking and build planning during `pnpm install`. Package binary targets and shebang runtimes are now precalculated during tarball extraction and served in `pnpr` registry metadata alongside verified `requiresBuild`, tarball size, and file-count metadata.

- Lowered peak memory when pnpm downloads many packuments, such as during lockfile verification with `trustPolicy` on Linux. In one 1,800-entry workspace, a lockfile update now peaks at 1.8 to 2.0 GB. It peaked at 2.6 to 3.7 GB before [#​17020](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17020).

- `pnpm install` in a Cargo workspace skips crates that an earlier install already unpacked into the store. Before, a repeat install processed every crate in `Cargo.lock` again. `pnpm install --force` unpacks every crate again [pnpm/tasks#69](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/69).

##### Linking node_modules and workspaces

- Concurrent installs that import the same package into one project now all complete. One of them used to fail with `ENOTEMPTY` when its copy of the package collided with the copy another install had already placed [pnpm/tasks#48](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/48).

- `pnpm install` now succeeds when `node_modules` is a symlink to an existing directory. Dependency hoisting previously rejected a symlinked `node_modules` as an invalid destination [#​17157](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17157).

- A filtered first install under the isolated linker now links every workspace project by name into `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules`, not only the selected ones [pnpm/tasks#155](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/155).

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a filtered install such as `pnpm --filter app add <pkg>` keeps the root `node_modules` links and bins of the workspace projects it did not select. A project with no dependencies of its own lost them until the next full install.

- `pnpm install --filter` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `--prod` or `--dev` now preserves previously installed dependency groups for unselected workspace projects [pnpm/tasks#164](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/164). Repeat filtered installs also re-resolve when a transitive injected workspace dependency or a linked dependency's version changes.

- With `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm install` now runs the workspace root's pnpmfile for every project, after the project's own pnpmfile. Before, it ran only the pnpmfile in the project's directory.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm peers check` now detect peer dependency issues and report linked package versions in linked projects that use `package.json5` or `package.yaml` [pnpm/tasks#172](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/172).

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm peers check` no longer report an unmet peer when a workspace package's peer is provided by a remote tarball URL. pnpm now compares the peer range with the version in the tarball's manifest [#​17037](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17037).

- `pnpm prune` now removes extraneous direct packages from `node_modules` when `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are already in sync. `pnpm prune` also honors `--filter`, `--recursive`, `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, and the `trustLockfile` setting and `--trust-lockfile` flag. With the lockfile trusted, `pnpm prune --prod` works offline when every package is in the store [#​16999](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16999).

##### Injected workspace packages

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` when a local directory dependency or injected workspace package changes a dependency to a different tarball URL or git commit [#​17129](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17129). It also fails when an injected workspace package changes a dependency's named-registry range, such as `work:^2.0.0`, to one the locked version no longer satisfies.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts the lockfile it wrote for a `file:` dependency on a directory without a `package.json`. It also accepts the lockfile for an injected workspace package that bundles a dependency in `bundledDependencies`, lists a dependency in both `dependencies` and `optionalDependencies`, or publishes from a `publishConfig.directory` whose `package.json` lists other dependencies than the project's own. Before, these failed with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`.

- The lockfile now records a `catalog:` peer dependency of an injected workspace package as written in its `package.json`. It recorded the catalog's range before, so editing the catalog changed the consumer's lockfile entry [pnpm/tasks#153](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/153).

- `pnpm install` now resolves a git, tarball, or tag dependency of an injected workspace package again when its spec changes. Before, it kept the old version.

- Repeat installs and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now re-check projects that inject a modified workspace package, including when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [#​17007](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17007), and accept aliased `workspace:` ranges on linked dependencies.

- An injected workspace package that was linked now becomes a copy when the project that depends on it starts providing one of its peers at a version the package's own workspace context lacks. The link used to stay until that dependency was updated, so the package could not find the peer the project provides [#​17057](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17057).

- An injected workspace package now keeps only the files its manifest lists after a lifecycle script or a script named in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` rebuilds it. Before, these refreshes copied every file of the package directory into the injected copy, including files that `files` or `.npmignore` leave out. With `deployAllFiles: true` the copy still gets every file.

- A script listed in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` now keeps a package's links to its own files as links in the injected copies, the way `pnpm install` writes them, and updates those copies when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. Before, a directory link the script added became a real directory or went missing with `deployAllFiles`, and with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` the copies kept the files from the last install.

##### Running scripts and checking dependencies

- Pressing Ctrl+C during `pnpm -r run` or `pnpm --filter <pkg> run` no longer reports 

> [!IMPORTANT]
> ✂ PR body was truncated to here.


</details>

### Configuration and setting up pnpm

- Registry credentials and TLS settings passed with `--config`, such as `--config.//registry.example.com/:_authToken=<token>`, are now applied. They take precedence over the same settings in `.npmrc` files.

- pnpm now reads only the settings it needs to decide whether to switch to the pnpm version a project pins. A setting outside them can no longer fail that decision or change its outcome. For example, `pnpm --version` no longer fails in a pinned project whose `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has a setting this pnpm cannot read. Projects that pin neither pnpm nor a runtime skip this check without reading any settings.

- When pnpm switches to the version a project pins, an option only the pinned pnpm knows now reaches that pnpm when it comes immediately before the command name, as in `pnpm --new-flag install`. When switching for `pnpm --version` or an unrecognized command line, pnpm also honors `--color`, `--no-color`, `--reporter`, and `--loglevel` wherever they appear on the command line.

- `pnpm self-update` now updates the project's pnpm pin when Homebrew installed pnpm or Corepack runs it, leaving the global pnpm alone [#​17001](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17001). Run inside a workspace package, `pnpm self-update` updates the pin in the workspace root's manifest, including in `package.yaml` or `package.json5`.

- `pnpm setup` now completes when Windows registry environment values cannot be read or written. It prints PowerShell commands to configure `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` without registry access [#​17167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17167).

- `pnpm setup` now succeeds when it cannot tell which shell configuration file to update, for example in a container where `SHELL` is not set. It installs pnpm and prints the `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` lines to add yourself. Previously it failed with `ERR_PNPM_UNKNOWN_SHELL`, and so did the installer script at get.pnpm.io [#​16973](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16973).

- In StackBlitz WebContainers, `pnpm` no longer crashes intermittently with `Parking not supported on this platform`, and running a command that does not exist now reports that the command was not found. Previously it sometimes failed with a generic error.
