### [`v12.14.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.14.0): pnpm 12.14.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.13.0...v12.14.0)

This release adds the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting, stops `pnpm install` from waiting on the daily update check, and keeps pnpm from aborting with a core dump when the reader of its output exits.

##### Minor Changes

- Added the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting for packages whose build depends on something pnpm cannot include in the cache key, such as the system libraries a native addon links against. pnpm builds the listed packages in every project and never restores or saves their builds through the side-effects cache, locally or on a `remoteCache` server. Under the global virtual store, each project gets its own copy of these packages and of the packages that depend on them. Entries use the same `name`, `@scope/*`, and `name@version` patterns as `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` [#​5271](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5271).

- `pnpm login` now prints the `npm-notice` response header during web-based login. Registries use it to show the verification code that completes the sign-in in the browser.

##### Patch Changes

##### Installing packages

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm add` no longer wait for the daily update check. If the command finishes first, pnpm skips the update notice and checks again next time. On a registry that accepted the connection but never answered, an install that had nothing to do used to take minutes [#​16839](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16839).

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm add` and `pnpm update` now reuse `pnpm-lock.yaml` when the workspace configures a catalog entry that no dependency references, such as an unused entry or one whose package an `overrides` entry replaces. Before, every resolution in such a workspace resolved all dependencies again from the registry [#​16923](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16923).

- `pnpm install` now looks up a git dependency's branch or tag once per install, even when many workspace projects depend on it. With `linkWorkspacePackages` enabled, it used to run `git ls-remote` once per project [#​16899](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16899).

- A filtered install, such as `pnpm install --filter <pkg>`, now keeps the `pnpm-lock.yaml` entries of workspace projects that are missing from disk, as in a sparse checkout. Their importers, packages, and catalog entries stay even when the filter matches every project on disk [#​16931](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16931).

- pnpm now decides whether a dependency that a package also declares as an optional peer is linked as a dependency or as a peer from the shallowest path that reaches the package. When an existing lockfile records such a dependency as a regular dependency and a newly added dependency now provides the peer, pnpm records it as a peer, as a fresh install does. The lockfile entry of such a package can change on the next install [#​16901](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16901).

- An install that adds nothing to the store no longer changes the modification time of the store directory. CI caches that check modification times, such as GitLab's, no longer re-upload an unchanged store [#​16929](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16929).

##### Running commands and scripts

- pnpm no longer aborts with a core dump when the reader of its output has exited, as in `pnpm list | head -1` or `pnpm start 2>&1 | head -1`. The command finishes with its usual exit code, and a failing script's exit code is kept. A write to stdout that fails for another reason, such as a full disk, ends the command with exit code 1 [#​16904](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16904) [pnpm/tasks#132](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/132).

- On Windows, `pnpm exec`, `pnpm run`, and commands such as `pnpm nx` now return when the command they run exits, even if it left a detached process running and pnpm's output is redirected or piped. Previously a shell reading that output waited until the detached process, such as the Nx daemon, exited [#​16930](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16930).

- Commands that do not write the project manifest now leave a missing `package.json` absent. This covers queries such as `pnpm why` and `pnpm outdated`, `pnpm fetch`, `pnpm dedupe --check`, and commands that exit with an error, such as `pnpm rt ls`. These commands used to create one from the initialization template. `pnpm sbom` run from a lockfile alone now reports the root component as `unknown` with version `0.0.0` [#​16907](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16907).

- `pnpm run` now reports a failed script as a JSON record under `--reporter=ndjson`. It printed a plain `[ELIFECYCLE]` line to stderr.

- `pnpm run` no longer prints `[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code N.` to stderr when a script fails under `--reporter=silent`, `--silent`, or `--loglevel=silent`.

- `pnpm pipeline --dry-run` no longer writes a run report when no projects are selected. With `--json` it prints `{"tasks": []}` [pnpm/tasks#126](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/126).

##### Packing and publishing

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now ship the whole gitignored directory that `main`, `browser`, or `bin` points into, as npm does. Previously only the `main` and `bin` files themselves were packed, and a gitignored `browser` file was left out [#​16908](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16908).

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now honor a `.npmignore` or `.gitignore` inside a subdirectory when `package.json` has a `files` field. The package root's ignore files and those inherited from the workspace are still skipped [#​16909](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16909).

##### Setting up pnpm and toolchains

- `--registry`, `--https-proxy`, `--http-proxy`, and `--no-proxy` now apply when pnpm resolves and downloads the pnpm version a project pins in `packageManager`. Before, these lookups went to `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, which a firewall that only allows a private registry blocks [#​16911](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/16911).

- On Windows, `pnpm install` now installs the Rust toolchain for rustup's default host, so a machine set up with `rustup set default-host x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` gets the MinGW toolchain. Without a default host, pnpm installs the MSVC toolchain for the machine's architecture, as rustup does. This includes a pnpm built for MinGW, such as the MSYS2 package, which has installed the MinGW toolchain since 12.13.0. An x64 pnpm on ARM64 Windows now installs the ARM64 toolchain [#​16854](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16854).

### [`v12.13.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.13.0): pnpm 12.13.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.12.1...v12.13.0)

This release adds the `pnpm profile` and `pnpm token` commands, the `storeIndexFormat: files` setting for stores shared over a network filesystem, and faster Python dependency resolution.

##### Minor Changes

- Added the `pnpm profile` command to view and update registry user profile settings.

- Added `pnpm token` to list, create, and revoke authentication tokens on the registry.

- Added the `storeIndexFormat` setting. Set it to `files` to keep a store's package index as one file per package instead of the SQLite `index.db`, for a store on a network filesystem that several machines use at once. SQLite's locking does not work across machines, so concurrent installs on such a store could corrupt `index.db`.

- Added the `nodePackageMap` setting, which groups the package-map settings. `nodePackageMap.mode: write-only` writes `node_modules/.package-map.json` for other tools without making Node.js load it. `mode: load` also makes Node.js load the map, like `nodeExperimentalPackageMap: true`. `nodePackageMap.type` replaces `nodePackageMapType`. The old settings still work [#​14937](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14937).

  ```yaml
  nodePackageMap:
    mode: write-only
    type: loose
  ```

##### Patch Changes

##### Setting up pnpm

- `pnpm setup` now works when pnpm was installed with npm on macOS. It installed pnpm from npm's `bin` directory and left a `$PNPM_HOME/bin/pnpm` that could not run [#​16855](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16855).

- pnpm runs again after `pnpm setup` when `globalShims` enables pnpm. Every command failed with "the global target of the pnpm shim points back at the shim" [#​16874](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16874).

- A pnpm built for the MinGW target on Windows, such as the MSYS2 package, now installs the MinGW Rust toolchain that `rust-toolchain.toml` names. It used to install the MSVC toolchain.

##### Installing packages

- On macOS, `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_WRITE_FILE` when the project is on a virtiofs or SMB share. pnpm now falls back to a regular `fsync` when the file system rejects a full sync [#​16846](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16846).

- On macOS, `pnpm install`, `pnpm patch-commit`, and other commands that load a pnpmfile no longer hang at random.

- `pnpm install` now puts the executables of a Python build backend's requirements on the `PATH` while the backend runs. Projects built with `uv_build` now install. Before, they failed with "uv-build was not properly installed".

- Removing a `link:` dependency now also removes its symlink from `node_modules` when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted` [#​16884](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16884).

- `pnpm-lock.yaml` no longer records the tarball URL of a package installed from a scoped registry, such as one set by `@types:registry=`, when pnpm can rebuild the URL from that registry [#​16866](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16866).

##### Packing, auditing, and pipelines

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now pack only `package.json`, the README, the license, and the files named in `main` and `bin` when `files` is an empty array. They used to pack every file in the package [#​16889](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16889).

- `pnpm audit` and `pnpm audit signatures` no longer check runtimes installed through `devEngines.runtime`, such as `node@runtime:24.21.0`, against the npm package of the same name. `pnpm audit signatures` reported these runtimes as having an invalid registry signature [#​16869](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16869).

- `pnpm pipeline` now runs the root's tasks when `pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists only the root in `packages` or omits `packages`, as `pnpm -r run` does. A change to a root file in such a workspace no longer triggers a full-run warning. When a full run has no projects to run, `pnpm pipeline` now reports that no projects are selected [#​16849](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16849).

##### Performance

- `pnpm install` resolves Python dependencies faster. With `--lockfile-only`, a project with 10 dependencies now resolves in about 4 seconds, down from about 40. When the index publishes a metadata file beside each wheel (PEP 658), as PyPI does, pnpm downloads only the wheels of the releases it selects.

- A repeat install against an existing lockfile no longer reads registry metadata for the dependencies it takes from that lockfile. On a warm store this removes thousands of metadata lookups from a repeat install of a large workspace.

- `pnpm install` with `enableModulesDir: false` now verifies the packages already in the store while the dependencies resolve, and checks a package's files in parallel. On a 5,100-package install with the store on a network filesystem, this removed a 19-second pause between resolution and fetching.

### [`v12.12.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.12.1): pnpm 12.12.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.12.0...v12.12.1)

This release adds OIDC authentication to `pnpm dist-tag` and the `tool:` protocol. `pnpm publish` now checks which registry an `NPM_ID_TOKEN` was issued for before using it.

##### Patch Changes

- `pnpm publish` now uses an `NPM_ID_TOKEN` only if its `aud` claim matches the selected registry, such as `npm:registry.npmjs.org`. A token for another registry is skipped with a warning, and pnpm falls back to the configured credentials.

- `pnpm dist-tag add`, `rm`, and `ls` now support OIDC authentication in CI. Enable "Allow npm dist-tag" in the package's trusted publishing settings to manage tags without a stored npm token.

- Added the `tool:` protocol for the tools pnpm downloads itself: Node.js, Bun, Deno, and Yarn. `pnpm add bun@tool:1.3.0`, `pnx node@tool:22`, and `pnx yarn@tool:4` work like the `runtime:` spelling, which stays supported as an alias. A lockfile written for `runtime:` stays up to date when `package.json` switches to `tool:`, and the other way around.

  A named registry can no longer be called `tool`.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk (@​modelcontextprotocol/server)</summary>

### [`v2.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/%40modelcontextprotocol/server%402.4.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/compare/@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.3.1...@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.4.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​3057](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3057) [`c05225a`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/c05225a636c679870b65f8ca4fe83a76ea1cf113) Thanks [@​steipete](https://redirect.github.com/steipete)! - `ServerEvent` takes optional `params`, which the `subscriptions/listen` router delivers with its own subscription ID, so a gateway can forward change notifications with their `_meta` and extension params.

- [#​3047](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3047) [`46d9c99`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/46d9c9921b6542e813c1ecc5f9fc964085e8e3bb) Thanks [@​KKonstantinov](https://redirect.github.com/KKonstantinov), [@​tobi-oye](https://redirect.github.com/tobi-oye), [@​mattzcarey](https://redirect.github.com/mattzcarey)! - Add the Skills extension (SEP-2640), reachable through new `ext/skills` subpaths; package root exports are unchanged.

  - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills`: `SkillsExtension` (`attach(server)` serves `skills/list`, `skills/get`, `resources/directory/read` and a `skill://{+path}` resource template), `SkillsExtension.load(files)` returning a `SkillCatalog` with `entries` and `reload()`, the `SkillFiles` storage adapter with `memorySkillFiles`, `SkillSource` for generated catalogs, `skillEntry`, and `SkillCatalogError`. Invalid skills are skipped with a warning (`onWarning`), or fail under `strict`. A file whose bytes are valid UTF-8 is served as `text`, whatever its MIME type; any other file as a base64 `blob`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/server/ext/skills/node`: `loadSkills(folder)` and `nodeSkillFiles(folder)`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/client/ext/skills`: `SkillsClient` with `list()` (throws on an invalid entry; `skipInvalid: true` keeps the valid ones and returns the rest in `invalid`), `get()`, `read(skill, path?)` (size, digest and `SKILL.md` frontmatter verified, `SkillVerificationError` on a mismatch; a copy from the response cache that fails a check is fetched once more with `cacheMode: 'refresh'` first) and `readDirectory()`.
  - `@modelcontextprotocol/core/ext/skills`: schemas, types and constants, including `SKILL_LIMITS`. The result schemas follow the stable spec, so `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` are required.

  `SkillsExtension.attach` is `@experimental`: how an extension is wired to a server may change in a minor release. The rest of the Skills API is stable.

  Works on 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28. On 2026-07-28 only, the server sends the caching fields (`ttlMs`, `cacheScope`), and `SkillsClient` requires them and returns them from `list()`, `get()` and `readDirectory()`.

##### Patch Changes

- [#​3083](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3083) [`ef38c67`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/ef38c6765a15ee29030340dfea28b013893fa0a2) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - The bundled Ajv validator is now built with fast-uri 3.1.8 (was 3.1.0). fast-uri 3.1.6 and later reject a `$id` or `$ref` whose text before the first colon is not a valid URI scheme (`my_tool:output`), or whose URN namespace is not valid (`urn:my_tool:output`): a schema that uses one no longer compiles, and a tool that carries it fails with an invalid-schema error. An underscore without a colon (`my_tool_output`) and a `$ref` into `#/$defs/...` or `#/definitions/...` are not affected.

- [#​2960](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2960) [`43c45f4`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/43c45f4941d824e7251a7d1266823a84af90fab3) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - A server whose tool puts `x-mcp-header` on a `number`-typed parameter keeps checking that tool's `Mcp-Param-*` headers on `tools/call`, as 2.3.0 does: a header that is missing for a value in the body, or that disagrees with the body, is answered `400` with JSON-RPC error `-32020`. Clients on a 2026-07-28 connection other than stdio no longer list such a tool and send no `Mcp-Param-*` headers for it, so a call that carries a value for a declared parameter is rejected the same way; the server logs a warning each time tools are listed. Use an integer (`z.int()`) or remove the annotation.

- [#​3081](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3081) [`5820f79`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/5820f796a48ae6b8e756a7fbfd627e7e2e1ac891) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - A tool `outputSchema` whose root is a `$ref` to a `type: "object"` entry of its own `$defs` or `definitions` (what zod writes for `z.object({...}).meta({ id })`), or a union of such refs, is now treated as an object schema. On 2025-era connections the tool's schema and `structuredContent` are no longer wrapped in `{ result: ... }`, so a 2025-era client that read `structuredContent.result` for such a tool now reads `structuredContent`. On every era the advertised schema gains `type: "object"` at its root.

- [#​3057](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3057) [`c05225a`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/c05225a636c679870b65f8ca4fe83a76ea1cf113) Thanks [@​steipete](https://redirect.github.com/steipete)! - Connecting a `Server` or `McpServer` to a `PerRequestHTTPServerTransport` classified at a modern revision that `supportedProtocolVersions` lists and the SDK implements now binds that revision, instead of answering `-32022`.

- [#​3005](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3005) [`b381559`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/b381559edc0dbe25ab8324cada345b49bd1d2fc4) Thanks [@​chaeyn](https://redirect.github.com/chaeyn)! - Reflect resource and resource template `update({ title })` changes in list responses. Preserve other metadata and individual resource titles when a template supplies list entries.

- [#​3002](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/3002) [`895007f`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/895007fe728b9c57fbe3ed45fe279ddc51f731f7) Thanks [@​Hugo-DDT](https://redirect.github.com/Hugo-DDT)! - `createMcpHandler` now sends `Allow: POST` on every `405` it answers to a non-POST request, with `legacy: 'stateless'` (the default) and with `legacy: 'reject'`.

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v12.15.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.15.0): pnpm 12.15

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.14.0...v12.15.0)

This release lets `pnpm-workspace.yaml` delegate settings to other files and config dependencies with `include`, adds `lockfile.integrityTarget: tar` and tar-registry support, accepts zstd-compressed registry responses, and honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` in `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install`. It also rejects registry metadata that names a different package than the one requested and speeds up workspace installs and macOS file linking.

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` can now delegate settings to other YAML files and to config dependencies through a new `include` field. Each source may define only the settings the root manifest delegates to it. Every setting has one owner. Commands that change settings write each one to the file that owns it. A relative path in an included file is relative to that file. See [Splitting Settings Across Files](https://pnpm.io/config-includes).

  A config dependency supplies its settings through the YAML file named in the `pnpm.config` field of its `package.json`. The new `bootConfig` setting sets the release-age and trust policy pnpm uses to install config dependencies and the pnpm version from `packageManager`.

- Added the `lockfile.integrityTarget` setting. With `integrityTarget: tar`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins the hash of every package's uncompressed tar, so the lockfile no longer changes when a registry recompresses its tarballs or serves them as tars. pnpm learns a version's tar hash from the store or by downloading it once. `pnpm audit signatures` ties the tar hash to the signed `.tgz` integrity.

  ```yaml title="pnpm-workspace.yaml"
  lockfile:
    integrityTarget: tar
  ```

- pnpm can now install from a registry that serves uncompressed tars with zstd or gzip content coding. `pnpm-lock.yaml` records the hash of each tar. Declare such a registry with `serverType: pnpr` in `registries` to keep tarball URLs out of the lockfile. See [Tar registries](https://pnpm.io/registries#tar-registries).

  pnpm now decodes the content coding of tarball downloads itself. It rejects a zstd response whose window is larger than 8 MiB.

  Added the `maxTarballUnpackedSize` setting. It caps the bytes the files of one package may unpack to, 4 GiB by default.

- Registry revisions now always pin the hash of the uncompressed tar, the original included. pnpm records an original selected through the revision protocol, for example with a `+r0` specifier, as `revision: 0` in the lockfile and fetches it from the registry's digest route. pnpm checks a revision's tar whether the registry sends it as a tar, gzip, or zstd. Revision metadata must list revision 0 and mark the selected revision. pnpm rejects incomplete revision metadata with `ERR_PNPM_MALFORMED_METADATA`.

- pnpm now accepts zstd-compressed responses. Registries that serve zstd send package metadata in fewer bytes than with gzip, most of all the full metadata that settings such as `minimumReleaseAge` and `trustPolicy` read.

- `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install` now use the `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable as an upper bound for timestamps in `node_modules/.modules.yaml` and `node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`. With an equivalently prepared deploy target and an epoch no later than the timestamps that would otherwise be recorded, deploying the same project twice produces identical files [#​17171](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17171).

- `pnpm update --interactive` now highlights the row under the cursor in cyan while keeping the colors of its version changes.

##### Patch Changes

##### Security

- pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_REGISTRY_NAME_MISMATCH` if a registry returns metadata for a package other than the one requested. Before, pnpm installed the package under the name in the metadata, so `allowBuilds` rules for the requested package did not apply to it.

- `minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune` and `trustPolicyExcludePrune` now keep exclusions for resolved configuration dependencies and their transitive dependencies [#​17142](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17142).

##### Resolving dependencies

- When `pnpm install` resolves a dependency again, it now reuses a version that the install already resolved for the same package, as a fresh install does. Before, it kept the version the lockfile pinned and added a second copy of the package. A locked version still stays when nothing else in the install prefers another version. To pin a transitive dependency on purpose, use `overrides` [#​17084](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17084).

- When another workspace project adds a different version of a package, a project's auto-installed peer on that package now moves to the version a fresh install picks. It used to stay on its locked version while any other project still accepted that version [#​17058](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17058).

- A package that lists the same dependency in `dependencies` and as an optional peer now gets the peer bound when a project adds a provider for it later. The lockfile now records every peer a package declares, including one its own dependency supplies [#​17056](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17056).

- `pnpm install --prod` and `pnpm deploy --prod` no longer drop a dependency that a package declares both as an optional peer and as its own dependency, when the package resolved it as its own dependency and a dev dependency provides the same package under another alias.

- `pnpm install` with an existing lockfile and a second `pnpm dedupe` now keep optional peer bindings that point into a dependency cycle or back into the dependent package. Before, the second run dropped the optional peer binding from the lockfile snapshot key.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` now preserve own-dependency and peer-dependency bindings when reusing a lockfile whose peer suffixes were hashed by `peersSuffixMaxLength`.

  Upgrading a direct dependency in one workspace project now refreshes matching transitive pins in sibling projects during the same `pnpm install` pass.

- With `resolvePeersFromWorkspaceRoot: false`, a workspace project no longer binds a peer to a version that only another project's dependencies provide. pnpm now auto-installs a version that satisfies the peer range for that project. Before, the project got a version outside the range, with no peer warning.

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm add`, and `pnpm update` now reuse the lockfile's resolution for dependencies that take part in a dependency cycle, such as `mlly` and `pkg-types`. They re-resolved those packages and everything that depends on them from the registry before [pnpm/tasks#130](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/130).

- pnpm now measures a `pnpm.overrides` entry written as a `workspace:` path, such as `workspace:./packages/foo`, from the directory holding `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. It used to be measured from each package the override rewrote. The install then linked a directory that does not exist, or failed if workspace packages were injected [#​17010](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17010).

- `pnpm install` now removes config dependencies that are no longer declared, including when the entire `configDependencies` setting is removed. Frozen installs reject a lockfile that still records removed config dependencies.

- `pnpm install --update-checksums` now re-resolves every locked package and records the integrity the registry reports now.

- `pnpm add` and `pnpm install` now accept `gist:<id>` dependencies and GitHub Gist URLs, and install them from the gist's archive. `pnpm pkg fix` normalizes a `gist:` repository the way `npm pkg fix` does, `pnpm licenses` links a gist package to its gist page, and `pnpm sbom` reports the repository of a package whose `repository` field is a `gist:` shorthand.

- `pnpm add` now reads the package name correctly from a tarball URL under a registry URL that has a path, such as `https://example.com/npm/`, and installs a registry tarball URL with a malformed percent escape as a plain tarball URL. Before, the registry path became part of the name, so a scoped package failed with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_PACKAGE_NAME`.

- With `minimumReleaseAge` set, pnpm now revalidates a package's cached full metadata with a single ETag request so an unchanged registry answers with `304`, even when the registry does not list a publish time for every version. Previously, pnpm downloaded that metadata again whenever the cached copy was older than `minimumReleaseAge`. With `resolutionMode` set to `lowest-direct` or `time-based`, pnpm also reuses that metadata across every workspace project that depends on the package.

- When pnpm revalidates cached registry metadata, it now sends `If-Modified-Since` when the registry's modification time is a date without a time, and no longer crashes when the modification time is before 1970.

- Added protocol versioning between the pnpm client and pnpr server, verified applied resolution policies in resolution responses, and preserved structured error codes across the wire.

##### Performance

- Sped up `pnpm install` on macOS. On a 12-core Mac, installing 1352 packages from a warm store took 1.3 seconds, down from 2.2. pnpm now writes package files into `node_modules` with 4 threads on macOS, whatever the number of CPU cores. Set the `PNPM_MACOS_LINK_THREADS` environment variable to use a different number of threads, or to `0` to write files with the threads pnpm uses for the rest of the install.

- `pnpm install` is faster and uses less memory in large workspaces with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. Each project's install no longer reads the manifests of every other workspace project again. Installs that wait for their workspace dependencies now count toward `workspaceConcurrency` [#​16966](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16966).

- Sped up workspace project discovery, dependency resolution, lockfile up-to-date checks, and peer dependency checks in large workspaces [#​16839](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16839) [pnpm/tasks#9](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/9). On a workspace with 6,833 projects, the lockfile up-to-date check uses about 1 second less CPU time. The peer dependency check at the end of an install now checks linked workspace projects against the manifests already in memory, without reading each `package.json` again.

- Sped up bin linking and build planning during `pnpm install`. Package binary targets and shebang runtimes are now precalculated during tarball extraction and served in `pnpr` registry metadata alongside verified `requiresBuild`, tarball size, and file-count metadata.

- Lowered peak memory when pnpm downloads many packuments, such as during lockfile verification with `trustPolicy` on Linux. In one 1,800-entry workspace, a lockfile update now peaks at 1.8 to 2.0 GB. It peaked at 2.6 to 3.7 GB before [#​17020](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17020).

- `pnpm install` in a Cargo workspace skips crates that an earlier install already unpacked into the store. Before, a repeat install processed every crate in `Cargo.lock` again. `pnpm install --force` unpacks every crate again [pnpm/tasks#69](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/69).

##### Linking node_modules and workspaces

- Concurrent installs that import the same package into one project now all complete. One of them used to fail with `ENOTEMPTY` when its copy of the package collided with the copy another install had already placed [pnpm/tasks#48](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/48).

- `pnpm install` now succeeds when `node_modules` is a symlink to an existing directory. Dependency hoisting previously rejected a symlinked `node_modules` as an invalid destination [#​17157](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17157).

- A filtered first install under the isolated linker now links every workspace project by name into `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules`, not only the selected ones [pnpm/tasks#155](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/155).

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a filtered install such as `pnpm --filter app add <pkg>` keeps the root `node_modules` links and bins of the workspace projects it did not select. A project with no dependencies of its own lost them until the next full install.

- `pnpm install --filter` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `--prod` or `--dev` now preserves previously installed dependency groups for unselected workspace projects [pnpm/tasks#164](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/164). Repeat filtered installs also re-resolve when a transitive injected workspace dependency or a linked dependency's version changes.

- With `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm install` now runs the workspace root's pnpmfile for every project, after the project's own pnpmfile. Before, it ran only the pnpmfile in the project's directory.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm peers check` now detect peer dependency issues and report linked package versions in linked projects that use `package.json5` or `package.yaml` [pnpm/tasks#172](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/172).

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm peers check` no longer report an unmet peer when a workspace package's peer is provided by a remote tarball URL. pnpm now compares the peer range with the version in the tarball's manifest [#​17037](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17037).

- `pnpm prune` now removes extraneous direct packages from `node_modules` when `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are already in sync. `pnpm prune` also honors `--filter`, `--recursive`, `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, and the `trustLockfile` setting and `--trust-lockfile` flag. With the lockfile trusted, `pnpm prune --prod` works offline when every package is in the store [#​16999](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16999).

##### Injected workspace packages

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` when a local directory dependency or injected workspace package changes a dependency to a different tarball URL or git commit [#​17129](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17129). It also fails when an injected workspace package changes a dependency's named-registry range, such as `work:^2.0.0`, to one the locked version no longer satisfies.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts the lockfile it wrote for a `file:` dependency on a directory without a `package.json`. It also accepts the lockfile for an injected workspace package that bundles a dependency in `bundledDependencies`, lists a dependency in both `dependencies` and `optionalDependencies`, or publishes from a `publishConfig.directory` whose `package.json` lists other dependencies than the project's own. Before, these failed with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`.

- The lockfile now records a `catalog:` peer dependency of an injected workspace package as written in its `package.json`. It recorded the catalog's range before, so editing the catalog changed the consumer's lockfile entry [pnpm/tasks#153](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/153).

- `pnpm install` now resolves a git, tarball, or tag dependency of an injected workspace package again when its spec changes. Before, it kept the old version.

- Repeat installs and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now re-check projects that inject a modified workspace package, including when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [#​17007](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17007), and accept aliased `workspace:` ranges on linked dependencies.

- An injected workspace package that was linked now becomes a copy when the project that depends on it starts providing one of its peers at a version the package's own workspace context lacks. The link used to stay until that dependency was updated, so the package could not find the peer the project provides [#​17057](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17057).

- An injected workspace package now keeps only the files its manifest lists after a lifecycle script or a script named in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` rebuilds it. Before, these refreshes copied every file of the package directory into the injected copy, including files that `files` or `.npmignore` leave out. With `deployAllFiles: true` the copy still gets every file.

- A script listed in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` now keeps a package's links to its own files as links in the injected copies, the way `pnpm install` writes them, and updates those copies when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. Before, a directory link the script added became a real directory or went missing with `deployAllFiles`, and with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` the copies kept the files from the last install.

##### Running scripts and checking dependencies

- Pressing Ctrl+C during `pnpm -r run` or `pnpm --filter <pkg> run` no longer reports `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL`. pnpm now ends with the interrupted script's status, such as 130 for a script that SIGINT ended on Linux or macOS [#​16964](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16964).

- With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, a Node.js resolve hook that a script registers now sees the importer as `context.parentURL` after pnpm's `NODE_PATH` fallback fails to find a bare specifier. Hooks that resolve tsconfig `paths` aliases from the importer failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` [#​16979](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16979).

- `pnpm run`, `pnpm exec`, and `pnpm restart` now pass the install flags they were given, such as `--lockfile-dir`, `--modules-dir`, `--store-dir`, `--offline`, and `--ignore-scripts`, to the `pnpm install` that `verifyDepsBeforeRun: install` starts. When that install leaves the dependencies out of date, pnpm now prints a warning.

- A repeated `pnpm install --filter` now finishes without reinstalling when the selected projects are up to date, and so does `pnpm install` once filtered commands have installed every project. After a filtered install, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now install a selected project whose dependencies changed in between [#​17011](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17011), require the workspace root when a filtered install with `pruneDirectDependencies: true` skipped it [pnpm/tasks#181](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/181), and preserve the recorded ignored build scripts of unselected projects.

- The check that runs before a script now holds the workspace projects that the selected project depends on, including with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` and for workspace dependencies declared with `link:`. `--filter=<project>...` now selects `link:` dependencies as well. In a workspace that has no `package.json` at its root, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer reinstall before every command when the dependencies are up to date.

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` and repeat `pnpm install` runs now apply `overrides` before comparing a modified `package.json` with `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#​17127](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17127). `pnpm install` with `optimisticRepeatInstall` now re-runs when `configDependencies` changed, `verifyDepsBeforeRun` reports `node_modules` out of date when `useGitBranchLockfile` is enabled and the branch lockfile is missing, and in a single-project repository both checks record a successful lockfile check so later runs skip it until the lockfile changes [#​16993](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16993).

- `pnpm install` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now compare manifests, lockfiles, and patch files by content hash. They notice an edit that kept the file's modification time, as `cp -p`, `rsync -a`, or an archive extraction leave it, and a patch file that was copied or touched without changing its content no longer marks dependencies as outdated [#​16988](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16988).

##### Deploying, packing, and other commands

- `pnpm deploy` now deploys `file:` dependencies that live outside the workspace directory. It failed with "Refusing to deploy unsafe lockfile path" [#​16983](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16983).

- `pnpm deploy` now records the peer dependencies of the workspace packages it copies into the deployed lockfile. Before, pnpm rejected that lockfile with `--frozen-lockfile` when a deployed workspace package declared a peer and `injectWorkspacePackages` was off [#​17093](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17093).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now succeed inside a directory created by `pnpm deploy`. `pnpm deploy` writes self-contained workspace and lockfile settings, prunes unused `patchedDependencies`, and preserves workspace-level dependency resolutions on deployed directory dependencies.

- On macOS, `pnpm deploy` no longer writes a second, unused copy of every package to `node_modules/.pnpm/@` in the deploy directory [#​17116](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17116).

- `pnpm patch-commit` and `pnpm install` now apply a patch that renames or moves a file of the patched package. Such a patch failed with "rename/copy operations in patches are not yet supported".

- In workspaces with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm patch`, `pnpm patch-commit`, and `pnpm patch-remove` now resolve patch files and `patchedDependencies` entries at the workspace root. `pnpm install` checks configured patches across all workspace projects before reporting unused patches.

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` no longer include editor swap files such as `.*.swp`, macOS `._*` files, `.lock-wscript`, `.wafpickle-*`, `build/config.gypi`, or `archived-packages/` in the tarball. Naming one of these files in `files` still includes it [#​16955](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16955).

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now support extended glob patterns and brace ranges such as `part{1..3}.js` and `part{a..c}.js`, including descending ranges, steps, and zero padding, in `files`, `.npmignore`, and `.gitignore`. Explicitly listed internal directory symlinks are preserved below excluded directories, entry points honor nested ignore files, ignore negations can re-include default-excluded logs and backup files, and nested lockfiles follow the package's file selection rules.

- Trusted publishing with OIDC now works with registries whose URL has a path, such as `https://registry.example/npm/private/`. pnpm previously sent the token exchange request to the root of the registry host.

- `pnpm deprecate` and `pnpm unpublish` now work for packages whose registry metadata is larger than 10 MiB, such as `typescript`. They accept up to 50 MiB, the same limit as `pnpm owner`.

- `pnpm owner ls` now lists the owners of a package on the npm registry. It reported every package as not found.

- `pnpm licenses list --prod` now includes optional dependencies, including transitive ones. Pass `--no-optional` to leave them out. `pnpm licenses list` also reports no licenses for workspace projects not recorded in the lockfile, errors when `pnpm-lock.yaml` is missing, and formats empty results as the requested text or JSON [pnpm/tasks#174](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/174).

- `pnpm why` now reads each selected workspace project's lockfile and modules directory when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#169](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/169).

- `pnpm pkg fix` now converts a `repository` string such as `github:pnpm/example` to the object form, as `npm pkg fix` does. It also normalizes a GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repository URL the way `npm pkg fix` does [#​16980](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16980).

##### Configuration and setting up pnpm

- Registry credentials and TLS settings passed with `--config`, such as `--config.//registry.example.com/:_authToken=<token>`, are now applied. They take precedence over the same settings in `.npmrc` files.

- pnpm now reads only the settings it needs to decide whether to switch to the pnpm version a project pins. A setting outside them can no longer fail that decision or change its outcome. For example, `pnpm --version` no longer fails in a pinned project whose `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has a setting this pnpm cannot read. Projects that pin neither pnpm nor a runtime skip this check without reading any settings.

- When pnpm switches to the version a project pins, an option only the pinned pnpm knows now reaches that pnpm when it comes immediately before the command name, as in `pnpm --new-flag install`. When switching for `pnpm --version` or an unrecognized command line, pnpm also honors `--color`, `--no-color`, `--reporter`, and `--loglevel` wherever they appear on the command line.

- `pnpm self-update` now updates the project's pnpm pin when Homebrew installed pnpm or Corepack runs it, leaving the global pnpm alone [#​17001](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17001). Run inside a workspace package, `pnpm self-update` updates the pin in the workspace root's manifest, including in `package.yaml` or `package.json5`.

- `pnpm setup` now completes when Windows registry environment values cannot be read or written. It prints PowerShell commands to configure `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` without registry access [#​17167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17167).

- `pnpm setup` now succeeds when it cannot tell which shell configuration file to update, for example in a container where `SHELL` is not set. It installs pnpm and prints the `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` lines to add yourself. Previously it failed with `ERR_PNPM_UNKNOWN_SHELL`, and so did the installer script at get.pnpm.io [#​16973](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16973).

- In StackBlitz WebContainers, `pnpm` no longer crashes intermittently with `Parking not supported on this platform`, and running a command that does not exist now reports that the command was not found. Previously it sometimes failed with a generic error.

<summary>sass/dart-sass (sass)</summary>

### [`v1.106.1`](https://redirect.github.com/sass/dart-sass/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#11061)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/sass/dart-sass/compare/1.106.0...1.106.1)

- Fix a bug where an attribute selector with an empty value (such as
  `[class=""]`) would crash when serializing.

- Don't crash when serializing a number with an empty unit. This is only
  possible through the JavaScript and Dart APIs or the embedded protocol.

##### Embedded Dart Sass

- More robustly convert invalid value errors into `PARAMS` errors.

### [`v1.106.0`](https://redirect.github.com/sass/dart-sass/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#11060)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/sass/dart-sass/compare/1.105.2...1.106.0)

- Don't normalize CSS escapes in statement contexts that can contain
  interpolation. For example, `@f\6Fo` is now emitted as written rather than
  normalized to `@foo`.

- Fix a bug where quotes would be removed from attribute selector values that
  contained backslashes.

- Fix invalid source spans that could cause crashes when encountering a syntax
  error in selectors or media queries that also contain escape sequences.

- Fix a bug where the indented syntax parser would crash when parsing a file
  where the first statement was indented *and* appeared after the first line.

- Fix a bug that could cause crashes when encountering errors or warnings in
  interpolations that contain patterns like `// */`.

- **Potentially breaking compatibility fix:** CSS escape codes whose values are
  0, for Unicode surrogates, or greater than the maximum allowed code point are
  now consistently normalized to U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER in expression
  contexts. Previously, in some cases these were instead normalized to the
  normalized form of the original escape sequence, which violates the principle
  that all escape sequences for identical values should be normalized the same
  way. In other cases, these would simply throw errors.

  As a special case, `\0` on its own will continue to be normalized to `\0 ` to
  support historical CSS hacks.

- **Potentially breaking bug fix:** Throw an error for mixins and functions that
  have rest parameters which are the same as normal parameters. Previously, the
  positional parameters wouldn't be accessible and calling such a mixin or
  function with a named argument would crash the compiler.

- **Potentially breaking bug fix:** Fix various cases where using a CSS escape
  code at the beginning of an identifier would change parsing behavior versus
  using the character directly.

- **Potentially breaking bug fix:** When a number's unit is ambiguous with a
  numeric exponent, the unit is now serialized as an escape code rather than a
  literal `e` to avoid being interpreted as an exponent by CSS.

- **Potentially breaking bug fix:** Don't parse a CSS escape code for U+45 LATIN
  CAPITAL LETTER E or U+65 LATIN LOWERCASE LETTER E as an exponent in
  `@keyframes` percentage selectors.

- **Potentially breaking bug fix:** Properly normalize underscores written as
  CSS escape codes in variable, mixin, and function names.

</details>

Issues.Title: fix(material/chips): avoid clipping icon avatars
Issues.Body: Icons used with matChipAvatar were clipped by the avatar's circular shape because mat-icon hides its overflow; the icon is now allowed to overflow so its corners render, while image avatars and app-styled backgrounds keep the avatar shape. The chips docs now state that the leading slot accepts icons, and icon spacing is left unchanged to avoid layout shifts. **Screenshots of before and after this change:** **Notes**: - The fix sets `overflow: visible` on `mat-icon` avatars instead of removing their `border-radius`. Removing the radius would turn app-styled circular icon backgrounds into squares (third screenshot). - `mat-icon` normally hides its overflow (#11826). Inside a chip, the leading slot already hides its own overflow and ignores pointer events, so that protection is kept. - Image avatars, text avatars, the selection checkmark, edit and remove buttons, and chip dimensions are unchanged. I checked this with computed styles and pixel diffs in M2 and M3, LTR and RTL, and dense layouts. - Icon spacing (the issue's 8px/8px point) is intentionally unchanged. Changing it would alter the width of every chip with an icon, and the same slot also holds the selection checkmark. Happy to handle it in a follow-up, if desired. Fixes #31628.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/chips): avoid clipping icon avatars" (#33991)

Issues.Title: docs(material/tabs): clarify when background and foreground tokens apply
Issues.Body:
Documents that the `background-color` and `foreground-color` tokens of `tabs-overrides` only
take effect together with the `backgroundColor` input, which is supported in M2 themes only,
and points to the tokens that customize the label and indicator colors in M3 themes.

Fixes #30186

Issues.Title: refactor(cdk-experimental/popover-edit): iterate map entries directly
Issues.Body: Removes an IE11 workaround that copied the map's keys into an array before iterating over them. Now that IE11 isn't supported, the entries can be iterated directly.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(cdk-experimental/popover-edit): iterate map entries directly" (#33987)

Issues.Title: docs: convert component styling tab to signals
Issues.Body:
Replaces the `async` pipe usages in the styling tab with signals. The token data of the `ComponentViewer.docItem` is loaded through an `httpResource` and the values derived from it are `computed` signals. Packages without token data don't make a request and indicate that they don't support style overrides, like before.

The token data is no longer cached by a service for the lifetime of the app, since it's loaded from static assets. Also adds tests for the styling tab, since it didn't have any.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs: convert component styling tab to signals" (#33986)

Issues.Title: docs: convert component viewer tabs to signals
Issues.Body:
Replaces the `async` pipe usages in the overview, API and examples tabs with signals. The tabs read the doc item from the `ComponentViewer.docItem` input and `showToc` is converted using `toSignal`.

The subscriptions that reset the table of contents when the doc item changes and that re-add its headers when it's shown again after a resize are replaced with an `effect` and an `afterRenderEffect`. Adds tests for both, since they weren't covered.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs: convert component viewer tabs to signals" (#33985)
